Your narrative

Your description of events

Im

| am filing this complaint to report corporate fraud, billing manipulation, and
severe beneficiary harm involving Medi-Cal Rx funds at CVS Pharmacy Store
#9785 (operated by Garfield Beach CVS, LLC at 2006 W Ave J, Lancaster, CA
93536).

| am a high-risk patient enrolled in a clinically supervised Diazepam taper
program. On April 20, 2026, at 9:05 AM, my healthcare provider electronically
transmitted a prescription for 5 MG Diazepam to this CVS location. Official
electronic transaction logs from Medi-Cal Rx (Chat Log Ref #311) confirm
that the government-funded program successfully authorized and paid for this
claim three separate times: at 9:06 AM, 9:40 AM, and 9:45 AM.

Despite the fact that the government had already authorized and funded the
transaction, an on-duty pharmacist identifying himself as "Randy" called me
from the pharmacy’s line (661-945-2729) at exactly 9:45 AM. He issued a verbal
constructive refusal, stating the pharmacy would not dispense the medication
until "tomorrow."

To override the government's approvals, CVS Store #9785 abused its billing
access by manually submitting system reversals to Medi-Cal Rx at the exact
time of the phone call (9:45 AM). They used their authorized coding access
deceptively -- falsifying the electronic record to claw back the state's payment
and make it look like the prescription could not be filled, all without medical
justification or provider consent.

This intentional 16-hour delay of a government-approved, life-sustaining
medication caused severe beneficiary harm. The forced interruption of my
supervised treatment caused acute autonomic distress, central nervous system
destabilization, severe physical tremors, and a total loss of consciousness. | was
unable to secure the medication until 1:01 AM on April 21, 2026.

CVS Store #9785’s deceptive use of manual billing reversals to cancel valid
government approvals constitutes an abusive manipulation of Medicaid/Medi-
Cal transaction systems and a dangerous breach of patient care. | possess full
supporting documentation, including the Medi-Cal Rx timestamp logs, phone
records, and medical necessity letters from my provider.
